title: Central Texas Council of Governments Awarded $548,000 Federal Grant - NewsBreak
text:
By Contributed Article ,
7 hours ago The Central Texas Council of Governments (CTCOG), in partnership with the Killeen– Temple Metropolitan Planning Organization (KTMPO), has been awarded $548,000 in federal funding through the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) Grant Program.
The funding will support the Central Texas Pilot Program for Safer Access to Schools and Safety Action Plan Update, a regional initiative focused on improving roadway safety and reducing serious injuries and fatalities, particularly for students traveling to and from school. The project was selected under the Fiscal Year 2025 SS4A Notice of Funding Opportunity and represents CTCOG’s second SS4A award.
The grant will cover the entire CTCOG region, including Bell, Coryell, Hamilton, Lampasas, Milam, Mills, and San Saba counties.
CTCOG and KTMPO previously received SS4A funding in Fiscal Year 2022 to develop the region’s first Safety Action Plan. This new award builds upon that work by updating the existing plan to meet current federal requirements and expanding safety efforts through supplemental planning and demonstration activities.
“This award allows us to take the next critical step in advancing roadway safety across Central Texas,” said Uryan Nelson, Director of Planning and Regional Services for CTCOG. “By updating our Safety Action Plan, piloting targeted safety improvements near schools, and identifying near-miss locations, we can better understand what strategies are most effective and guide future investments.”
The updated regional Safety Action Plan will also position local governments to compete for future federal and state safety funding, as a Safety Action Plan must be in place before jurisdictions can apply for SS4A implementation grants. By using a regional plan, cities and counties can meet this requirement without creating individual standalone plans.
Grant funding will support an update to CTCOG’s regional Safety Action Plan, supplemental planning focused on improving safer access to schools, and demonstration projects such as nearmiss analytics at ten trial locations and temporary deployment of safety countermeasures including leading pedestrian intervals, enhanced crosswalk markings, and rectangular rapid flashing beacons near schools.
These activities will be evaluated over a one-year period, with findings incorpoafter rated into the updated Safety Action Plan to guide future safety investments.
The total estimated cost of the project is $685,000, including a required 20 percent non-federal match, which will be provided through in-kind contributions. Federal funds will be administered following execution of a formal grant agreement with the Federal Highway Administration.
For more information about CTCOG’s transportation and safety initiatives, visit ktmpo.org, or learn more about the SS4A program at ctcog.org/ss4a.
